See AMC.U590
(a) The design of the Arresting System shall ensure that it retards the AV without imparting forces and accelerations in excess of those for which the airframe and its internal equipment are designed.
(b) The Arresting System shall accommodate deviations from the intended recovery trajectory resulting from local environmental conditions. (Wind, gust).
(c) The Arresting System shall include means to maintain UA azimuth on landing strip after touchdown and arresting hook engagement also in a situation in which one or both arresting devices (e.g. drums) fails to operate correctly.
(d) Arrested landings shall be performed to demonstrate that the aircraft can consistently engage the arresting gear and that aircraft motions during the arrested run-out are conducive to safe arrestment. The following where applicable shall be demonstrated:
  (1) That there is no cable impact damage to the aircraft during arrested landings for all landing conditions and landing configurations.
  (2) Satisfactory swivelling of the nose gear for rol1 back in the arresting gear.
  (3) Satisfactory anti-hunting and shimmy characteristics of the nose gear.
  (4) Abrupt application of brakes during the post arresting roll-back.
